lesson.title: How the pieces connect
lesson.summary: Web applications are built by connecting different files and modules together. When a user visits a page, the server fetches data and components, combining them to display the final view in the browser.
lesson.analogy: Think of a restaurant kitchen where the dining room (client) receives orders, the prep station (server) gathers ingredients from the pantry (database), and everything comes together to serve the customer. The limit of this analogy is that code execution happens instantly via digital networks rather than physical movement.

tutor.answer: Validation of note data is handled via a schema in the application code, ensuring strings meet specific length requirements before processing.

claims.text: The note body is validated using a Zod schema that enforces string trimming and length constraints.
The observed length limits require a minimum length of 1 character and a maximum length of 2000 characters.
API requests parse incoming JSON payloads using this note schema inside the POST route handler.
This validation code presence does not establish that runtime input handling is secure or that malicious inputs are entirely prevented across all client pathways.
